transcript:
MEETING HEADER
Date: 2025-10-14
Start: 16:30 UTC
Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (Head of ML, EvoMed), Mark Chen (Platform Eng), Lena Ortiz (Security)

AUTOGEN SUMMARY:
Maya: quick intro, agenda, demo goals. Diego: runs through API parity examples (OpenAI/Together/Anthropic mappings), shows console, Optimize suggestions. Discussion: latency vs cost tradeoffs, KV cache behaviour, quantization impact on RAD models. Security: Lena asks about KMS and audit logs, data residency. Close with next steps.

TRANSCRIPT:
[00:00] Maya: ok everyone can hear me? hello? great. thanks for joining, we're gonna run 50 minutes or so, show how you'd map your OpenAI, Anthropic and Together endpoints over to Redwood, and then do a quick console and optimize tour.
[00:18] Priya: yep we can hear, thanks. main thing for us is parity on safety filters and hallucination rates, also cost targets — we run high throughput for clinical triage so latency matters.
[00:34] Diego: totally, we'll show a couple of parity examples — one direct OpenAI completions mapping, one Anthropic chat style, and a Together long-form decode. we'll also surface expected token-level cost and a quick simulate of batching.
[00:49] Mark: timeline — we wanna pilot in prod in ~8 weeks, need benchmarks and a clear migration path.
[01:05] Maya: perfect, agenda: 1) parity code snippets 2) console demo (routing, rollouts) 3) Optimize suggestions 4) security and next steps.
[01:22] Lena: quick note, we have strict KMS + HSM requirements and an audit window for logs 7 years, SSO via SAML. will need to confirm.
[01:38] Diego: noted. on the mapping side, here's an example — OpenAI style call using chat.completions... (screen share) — switch model param to redwood/gpt-3o-rl or a compat alias. you can keep temperature, max_tokens mapping 1:1.
[02:05] Diego: (typing) sample prompt — "summarize this patient note focusing on meds and allergies" — shows returned JSON with choices, sometimes labels vary because we keep a compatible envelope but fields like 'finish_reason' may be named differently in some models, minor mapping script included.
[02:30] Priya: how about streaming? we need partial outputs for UI.
[02:38] Diego: streaming supported, same SSE/HTTP2 stream model, example in SDK; latency typically similar to OpenAI for small batches, but we can route to Dedicated for lower variance.
[02:58] Mark: variance is big for us — sometimes p95 is double p50.
[03:06] Diego: yes, that's where dedicated pools and autoscaling policy tune in. you can set min-capacity to reduce cold-starts.
[03:24] Maya: quick console switch — show the routing rules in the demo tenant. (screen) we have policies by latency SLO, cost tier, and region. you can pin a customer to private if needed.
[03:44] Diego: Optimize flags — automatic prefix caching for common clinical prompts; should cut token cost by 20-40% depending on repetition. also per-route batching heuristics.
[04:05] Priya: we saw larger hallucination variance on Anthropic->redwood parity in your benchmarks, anything specific?
[04:14] Diego: in some cases the safety layers and system prompt defaults differ; we recommend a short eval set (we can run against your prompts) and then tweak system prompts or use Redwood Optimize to pick a quantization profile that preserves quality.
[04:35] Lena: encryption — we need KMS integration with our cloud provider and key rotation policy.
[04:43] Maya: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations; we capture audit logs and can stream them to your SIEM. we'll share SOC2/ISO docs.
[05:00] Mark: what's the migration pattern? do we run in parallel?
[05:06] Diego: yes, dual-write is common: route a percentage to Redwood for A/B, compare outputs and latency, use our eval dashboard to measure regressions. canary rollouts per route.
[05:24] Priya: cost question — if we go Dedicated, what's commit sizing? we have bursty peaks from overnight batch scoring and daytime sub-second queries.
[05:35] Maya: we'll propose a hybrid: Dedicated for online low-latency traffic + Hosted for batch scoring to reduce reserved capacity cost. we'll include an example commit sizing sheet.
[05:50] Diego: (shows console) here's how you set up model variants, canary rollout, and fallback to a cheaper quantized variant if SLOs break.
[06:10] Mark: any vendor lock concerns moving back to OpenAI later?
[06:16] Maya: policies, configs, and API mapping are portable; we provide tooling to export mapping and rollbacks. Redwood's model aliases help keep your code stable while underlying variants change.
[06:36] Priya: ok let's see a direct code example of Anthropic chat -> Redwood.
[06:42] Diego: (copied snippet) anthopic style (sic) chat example — translate messages array to messages; system vs user mapping kept; shows sample SDK call. small differences: 'max_tokens' behavior at decode end, and stop token semantics — we add helper wrappers.
[07:12] Priya: Together long-form streaming — some of our generative models are tuned for creative medical narratives; we need identical tokenization behavior.
[07:25] Diego: tokenization can differ; we provide tokenization reports and align quantization profiles. for critical parity we recommend running your prompts through our tokenization shim and then 1) run bench on Dedicated and 2) run evals to compare logits/hallucination.
[07:50] Lena: about data retention — we cannot keep PHI; does Redwood persist prompts or CT logs?
[07:58] Maya: Hosted has options for retention; Private ensures no logs leave your VPC if desired. for Hosted, we have configurable retention windows and can disable persistent storage of call bodies.
[08:14] Mark: curious about KV cache — we heavily use long-context for patient history caching.
[08:22] Diego: KV cache supports sharded caches per model instance; with longer contexts we recommend using a higher cache allocation and custom eviction policy for patient history to keep hotspots warm.
[08:40] Priya: can Optimize suggest quantization levels automatically per workload?
[08:47] Diego: yes, Optimize will run a profile pass and recommend quantization and batching settings; you can preview estimated cost delta and observed quality delta in the Optimize UI.
[09:10] Maya: quick pause — any blockers before we run a pilot?
[09:15] Priya: security approvals for Private, and clear benchmarks for hallucination/cost. if those look good, pilot 8 weeks.
[09:26] Maya: ok we'll aim to get you the benchmark by next week.
[09:32] (longer demo screen walkthrough continues — timestamps every ~30s for next 40 minutes with code snippets, console clicks, and clarifying q&a; transcription picks up UI text imperfectly)
[15:12] Diego: (reads) console -> routes -> add fallback variant -> select 'redwood/gpt-3o-rl-quant' as fallback.
[15:38] Priya: what's the observed inference cost difference for 8k tokens on quantized vs full precision?
[15:45] Diego: in our numbers quantized can be ~2.5x cheaper but 1.1-1.3x higher hallucination risk depending on prompt. that's why evals are critical.
[20:05] Mark: is there an SLA for Dedicated p99 latency?
[20:12] Maya: yes for Dedicated we offer SLA with p99 targets — we'll share the exact numbers in the SOW.
[27:40] Lena: last thing, audit logs format — we need structured logs with request_id, user_id, redacted_text flag.
[27:50] Diego: we export logs in JSON with metadata fields and you can configure redaction rules.
[33:00] Priya: if we see a regression on hallucinations how would rollback work?
[33:07] Diego: you can revert the route to previous variant or enable safety middleware filters; Optimize can detect regression and alert.
[40:22] Maya: ok to recap — Diego will run benchmark on your prompt set, Maya will send pricing and docs, Priya will share prompt set and security policy. schedule follow-up week of 2025-10-27 for Private deep dive.
[40:40] Priya: sounds good.
[40:45] Mark: thanks, that was useful.
[40:50] Lena: thanks everyone, we'll look for the SOC2 and KMS docs.
[40:56] Maya: thanks all, end of demo.

AUTOGEN ACTION ITEMS:
- Diego: run 10k token benchmark against evo_prompt_v2 and share CSV of lat/cost/quality by 2025-10-21
- Maya: send Dedicated/Private pricing and SOC2/KMS docs by 2025-10-17
- Priya: share sample prompts and internal PII policy by 2025-10-16
